method: Manual classification of per-commit eval JSONs. Each D3≤0.25 buggy commit tagged with primary failure mode based on: (1) what the agent hypothesized vs ground truth, (2) whether the diff was truncated in the bug-relevant section, (3) whether the root cause required context beyond the diff.

d3_failure_classification.population: 10 buggy commits from n=20 stratified eval

commits.summary: Agent precisely identified negative default values rendered as positive due to JSON schema type-coercion.
Agent identified correct root cause in Hypothesis 3 (hardcoded constant vs resolved format variable) but didn't prioritize it as primary.

Agent focused on Host header NPE and duplicate headers in DefaultUndertowHttpBinding. Actual bug: UndertowProducer using full URL as request path (fix across URISupport.java + UndertowProducer.java). Agent saw the right file but reasoned about a different issue.
commits.could_context_help: Partially — seeing the fix-commit diff or blame on UndertowProducer.java might redirect attention, but the agent had the relevant file and still chose wrong mechanism.

commits.summary: Agent identified right area (EhcacheManager, concurrency) but missed actual fix: shared ReferenceCount CacheManager. Diff truncated at ~9KB, hiding the key EhcacheManager.java lifecycle logic.
commits.could_context_help: Yes — full diff or blame showing ReferenceCount utility would reveal the shared-lifecycle pattern.

commits.summary: Agent focused on whitespace/trim bug in enum parsing (CoreEipAnnotationProcessor.java). Actual bug: incorrect default values in 12 Spring Boot DataFormatConfiguration.java files. Agent reasoned from wrong file entirely.
commits.could_context_help: Unlikely — agent had the diff and chose to reason about an interesting-looking code pattern rather than the actual defect. The fix files (DataFormatConfiguration) were listed as touched but agent ignored them.

commits.summary: Agent found a REAL but DIFFERENT bug (TriggerKey null-variable substitution). Actual JIRA issue: trigger misfires from unconditional rescheduling with stale START_TIME. Agent found A bug but not THE bug.
commits.could_context_help: Unlikely — agent had the diff and found a plausible defect. The actual root cause (stale START_TIME in existing trigger) requires domain knowledge about Quartz scheduling semantics.

commits.summary: Diff truncated after XmppBinding.java and XmppConsumer.java. Actual bug in XmppGroupChatProducer.java (missing room password during reconnection). Agent couldn't see the relevant code.
commits.could_context_help: Yes — full diff would show the XmppGroupChatProducer.java changes where the bug lives.

commits.summary: Agent focused on binary incompatibility (generic type removal) and null serviceName NPE. Actual bug: Spring Boot deadlock during reactive-streams auto-configuration circular initialization. Fix files (ReactiveStreamsServiceAutoConfiguration, ServiceCreationHelper) not visible in agent's analysis.
commits.could_context_help: Possibly — Spring Boot auto-config lifecycle is architectural knowledge beyond diffs. Blame/history might show the circular dependency pattern. Test files would show deadlock reproduction.

commits.summary: JIRA issue has no description — judge cannot score D3. Agent's reasoning (code-gen without tests, 416-line Mojo) was plausible but untestable.
commits.could_context_help: N/A — judge infrastructure limitation, not agent failure.

commits.summary: 32-file commit (890 lines added), diff truncated at ~89KB. Agent focused on SmartLifecycle/ContextRefreshedEvent ordering. Actual bug: RoutesCollector fails to load Java DSL routes when XML routes present. RoutesCollector.java changes not visible.
commits.could_context_help: Yes — full diff showing RoutesCollector.java changes would reveal the mixed-routes handling bug.

wrong-mechanism.description: Agent had sufficient context but identified wrong defect mechanism. Prompt/reasoning issue.

missing-context-likely.description: Agent couldn't find root cause because relevant code was truncated (3) or required architectural context beyond the diff (1).

judge-infra.description: JIRA has no description — judge can't evaluate D3. Not an agent failure.

clean_fp_analysis.population: 10 clean commits from n=20 stratified eval
clean_fp_analysis.pattern: All 6 FP commits were classified HIGH with SUPPORTED hypotheses. Agent generates plausible, evidence-grounded defect hypotheses on clean commits. High D6 scores (1.0 on 5/6 FPs) confirm the agent IS grounding in the diff — it just reasons too aggressively.

fp_commits.mechanism: Cross-library NotifyingFuture substitution during Infinispan upgrade
Jetty binary incompatibility (crossed documented breaking threshold) + header behavior change
LogType/FileName label swap in structured log output
Not fully classified — likely similar pattern
Not fully classified — likely similar pattern
Not fully classified — likely similar pattern

clean_fp_analysis.key_insight: The rubric criterion (a) 'SUPPORTED hypothesis → HIGH' causes the agent to always classify HIGH when it finds any plausible defect. On clean commits, the agent finds plausible-looking patterns (type migrations, version bumps crossing documented thresholds, label mismatches) that look like real bugs but weren't. This is an inherent limitation of single-commit analysis without runtime or test evidence.

decision.recommendation: BOTH prompt refinement AND context expansion needed
rationale: 3/4 missing-context-likely cases are due to diff truncation specifically — increasing context_builder max_diff_chars would directly address these before needing test/blame expansion
60% clean-FP rate is a separate prompt issue — rubric criterion (a) is too aggressive on clean commits

iter_2_priority_order.action: Increase diff character limit in context_builder.py
iter_2_priority_order.expected_impact: Directly addresses 3/4 missing-context-likely cases (diff-truncation). Low cost, no LLM change.

iter_2_priority_order.action: Add clean-commit discrimination to rubric (e.g., require ≥2 SUPPORTED hypotheses for HIGH, or add MEDIUM-default for style/refactor commits)
iter_2_priority_order.expected_impact: Reduces 60% clean-FP rate. Directly improves D1 from 0.60 toward gate (0.70).

iter_2_priority_order.action: EXP-BUNDLE-EXPAND: add test files + blame snippets for INVESTIGATE-zone commits
iter_2_priority_order.expected_impact: Addresses architectural-depth case (90846b). May help wrong-mechanism cases by providing additional signal.

iter_2_priority_order.action: EXP-JUDGE-SWAP: cross-model judge to verify D3 scores aren't inflated
iter_2_priority_order.expected_impact: Mandatory before n=50 gate. Low cost.

decision.tier_2_verdict: PARTIALLY TRIGGERED. diff-truncation is a context-assembly fix (Priority 1), not a loop architecture change. True loop changes (EXP-BUNDLE-EXPAND) are justified but secondary to the simpler fix.
